# Sirach Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** The wisdom of the humble will lift up his head, and he shall be seated among great men.

**11:2** Do not praise a man for his beauty, nor despise a man for his appearance.

**11:3** The bee is small among flying creatures, yet her produce is the first of sweet things.

**11:4** Do not boast about your fine clothing, and do not exalt yourself on the day of your honor; for the works of the Lord are marvelous, and his works are concealed from men.

**11:5** Many kings have sat down upon the ground, but one never thought of has worn the crown.

**11:6** Many powerful men have been greatly humiliated, and those of renown have been delivered into the hands of others.

**11:7** Do not find fault before you investigate; understand first, and then correct.

**11:8** Do not answer before you have listened, and do not interrupt in the middle of speaking.

**11:9** Do not strive in a matter that is not your concern, and do not sit in judgment with sinners.

**11:10** My child, do not take on too many matters; if you multiply activities, you will not go unpunished; if you pursue, you will not overtake, and by fleeing you will not escape.

**11:11** There is one who labors, toils, and hurries, yet falls further behind.

**11:12** There is one who is slow, who needs assistance, who lacks ability, yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and he raised him up from his low estate.

**11:13** He lifted his head, and many were astonished at him.

**11:14** Good and evil, life and death, poverty and riches — all are from the Lord.

**11:15** The Lord's gift remains with the devout, and his favor leads to everlasting success.

**11:16** One person becomes wealthy through his careful diligence, and this is the portion of his reward.

**11:17** One person becomes poor through excessive frugality, and this is his appointed lot.

**11:18** There is one who grows rich through miserliness, and this is his reward:

**11:19** When he says, "I have found rest, and now I will enjoy my goods" — he does not know when the time will come when he will leave these things to others and die.

**11:20** Stand firm in your agreement and attend to it, and grow old in your work.

**11:21** Do not marvel at the deeds of a sinner; trust in the Lord and stay at your task; for it is easy in the eyes of the Lord to make a poor man suddenly rich.

**11:22** The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the devout, and in a moment he makes his blessing flourish.

**11:23** Do not say, "What do I need, and what benefit is there for me from now on?"

**11:24** Do not say, "I am self-sufficient, and what harm could happen to me now?"

**11:25** In the day of prosperity, adversity is forgotten; and in the day of adversity, prosperity is not remembered.

**11:26** For it is easy before the Lord to reward a person on the day of death according to his way.

**11:27** The misery of an hour makes one forget pleasure, and at the end, a man's deeds are revealed.

**11:28** Do not call anyone blessed before his death; a man will be recognized by his end, and by his children.

**11:29** Do not bring just anyone into your home, for many are the wiles of the crafty.

**11:30** Like a caged partridge used as a lure, so is the heart of the proud; and like a spy, he watches for your downfall.

**11:31** For he turns good things into evil, and on the praiseworthy he places blame.

**11:32** From a single spark a great fire is kindled, and a sinner lies in ambush for blood.

**11:33** Guard yourself against an evildoer, for he plots harm, lest he give you a lasting stain.

**11:34** Bring a stranger into your home and he will upset you with turmoil, and will alienate you from your own family.
